exports.description:
A confirmation that interrupts, usually before a destructive action: a modal
`<dialog role="alertdialog">` with a required description, a Cancel button that takes focus,
and your action. Esc cancels; a backdrop click never closes it. Shares Dialog's behaviour and
styles (`styles/AlertDialog.css` imports Dialog's). See `AlertDialog.a11y.ts`.

```tsx
<AlertDialog
  open={open}
  onOpenChange={setOpen}
  title="Delete project?"
  description="Its files and history are deleted. This can't be undone."
  cancelLabel="Cancel"
  action={<Button variant="danger" onClick={remove}>Delete</Button>}
/>
```
exports.name: AlertDialog

exports.description:
A native `<button>`, `type="button"` by default. See `Button.a11y.ts` for its accessibility
contract.
exports.name: Button

exports.description:
A native `<input type="checkbox">` with its own label, description and error. `className`
and `style` go on the row (`.senui-checkbox`); every other native attribute, and the ref, go on
the input. See `Checkbox.a11y.ts` for its accessibility contract.

```tsx
<Checkbox label="Email me about new releases" defaultChecked />
<Checkbox aria-label="Select all rows" checked={all} indeterminate={some} onCheckedChange={selectAll} />
```
exports.name: Checkbox

exports.description:
A `<fieldset>` and `<legend>` around a set of Checkboxes, with one description, one error and one
value array. The group's error is described on the fieldset only, so entering the group reads
legend and error once; each checkbox is `aria-invalid` while it shows.

```tsx
<CheckboxGroup legend="Topics" required="Choose at least one topic." defaultValue={['news']}>
  <Checkbox value="news" label="News" />
  <Checkbox value="releases" label="Releases" />
</CheckboxGroup>
```

See `CheckboxGroup.a11y.ts` for its accessibility contract.
exports.name: CheckboxGroup

exports.description:
A modal dialog: a native `<dialog>` opened with `showModal()`, so the page behind it is inert
and focus stays inside without a focus trap. Esc closes it; while it is open, the page doesn't
scroll (ADR-0014). The content renders only while it is open.
`className`, `style`, native attributes and the ref go on the `<dialog>`.
See `Dialog.a11y.ts` for its accessibility contract.

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
<Button onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Edit profile</Button>
<Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} title="Edit profile" closeLabel="Close">
  …
</Dialog>
```
exports.name: Dialog

exports.description:
Why a dialog asked to close. Open to new members in a minor, so a consumer switching on it keeps
a default branch.

`'forced'` is not a request: the browser has already closed the dialog. It does so on a second
Esc or back gesture with no user action in between, which a page may not refuse, or when code
calls `close()` on the element. Set `open` to false; refusing leaves it closed anyway.
exports.name: DialogCloseReason

exports.description:
A dialog is named by a visible `title`, or, with no visible heading, by exactly one of
`aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`. Never both.
exports.name: DialogName

exports.description:
The second argument of `onOpenChange`. A `<form method="dialog">` close carries the submitter's
`value`, read from the submit event, so it is never a stale `returnValue`.
exports.name: DialogOpenChangeDetails

exports.description:
`Omit` for union props. A plain `Omit<ButtonProps, 'variant'>` keeps only the keys every branch
shares, which collapses a discriminated union and drops type-level requirements such as an
icon-only button's accessible name. Use this when wrapping a senui component:

```tsx
type DangerButtonProps = DistributiveOmit<ButtonProps, 'variant'>;
```
exports.name: DistributiveOmit

exports.description:
Says there is nothing here, why, and what you can do: a heading, a description, a decorative
illustration and your actions. A plain `<div>` with no role and no live region. It adapts to the
width of its container, compact below 30rem and stacked above, so it takes the full inline size
of its parent: give a shrink-to-fit parent a width, and put inline margin on a wrapper.
`className`, native attributes and the ref go on the root.
See `EmptyState.a11y.ts` for its accessibility contract, including what your app must announce.

```tsx
<EmptyState
  headingLevel={2}
  title="No projects yet"
  description="Projects you create or join appear here."
  actions={<Button onClick={create}>Create project</Button>}
/>
```
exports.name: EmptyState

exports.description:
The heading's level. Required, with no default, because an empty state sits in your page's outline
and any default is wrong somewhere. No `1`: the page keeps its own `<h1>`.
exports.name: EmptyStateHeadingLevel

exports.description:
A label, optional description and error message for one form control, and the wiring between
them: the label's `for`, the control's `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid` and `required`. The
control is rendered by `children`, a function that receives the binding:

```tsx
<FormField label="Email" description="We reply here." error={errors.email} required>
  {(field) => <TextInput field={field} type="email" autoComplete="email" />}
</FormField>
```

See `FormField.a11y.ts` for its accessibility contract.
exports.name: FormField

exports.description:
What FormField hands its control: the ids and state that connect the control to the field's
label, description and error. It is sealed, so only FormField can make one, and a control given
one is named by the field's label (CONVENTIONS rule 3):

```tsx
<FormField label="Email">{(field) => <TextInput field={field} type="email" />}</FormField>
```
exports.name: FormFieldBinding

exports.description:
The shape of `components.json`, the machine-readable description of this package that ships in
it (`@senakster/senui/components.json`). This type is the schema: there is no JSON Schema.

```ts
import type { Manifest } from '@senakster/senui';
import manifest from '@senakster/senui/components.json' with { type: 'json' };

const button = (manifest as Manifest).components.Button;
```

Semver covers the set of components and their branches, prop names and whether each is
required, the values of variant props, data-attribute values, classes and component tokens.
Informative, and may change in any release: printed types, descriptions, dates, story ids and
URLs.

Enumerations are open: a value not listed here may appear in a minor release. Treat an unknown
value as "not described". `schemaVersion` changes only on a breaking change to this shape, in a
major release, after a release that emits the old and the new field side by side. Fields added
in a minor don't change it, so feature-detect them.

These are mirror types: they import nothing from the package's internals.
exports.name: Manifest

exports.description:
An on/off setting that takes effect at once: a native `<input type="checkbox" role="switch">`,
announced as a switch, toggled with Space or a click on its label. If the change only applies
when the user saves a form, use a Checkbox instead.
`className` and `style` go on the row (`.senui-switch`); every other native attribute, and the
ref, go on the input. See `Switch.a11y.ts` for its accessibility contract.

```tsx
<Switch label="Wi-Fi" checked={wifi} onCheckedChange={setWifi} />
```
exports.name: Switch

exports.description:
A native single-line `<input>`. Use it inside a FormField, which labels and describes it:

```tsx
<FormField label="Email" error={errors.email}>
  {(field) => <TextInput field={field} type="email" autoComplete="email" />}
</FormField>
```

Standalone (a search box with a visible button, say), name it with `aria-label` or
`aria-labelledby`. `value` / `defaultValue` / `onChange`, `autoComplete` and every other native
attribute pass through; paste is never blocked. See `TextInput.a11y.ts` for its accessibility
contract.
exports.name: TextInput

exports.description: Single-line text types. `number` is not one: it is a spin button, with its own role and keys.
exports.name: TextInputType
